key_insight: A single data-driven closure trained at the expected viscosity can be reused across random-viscosity realizations, with physical constraints improving reduced-order model accuracy and robustness.
engineering_relevance: The approach can reduce the computational burden of uncertainty quantification for unsteady incompressible flows without training a separate closure for every viscosity realization.
method: Combine POD reduced-order modeling, spatial filtering, and stochastic collocation.
Train a shared data-driven correction using the full-order solution at the expected viscosity.
Impose physical constraints in CDDC-UQ-ROM to improve robustness.
evidence_signal: Tests on 2D cylinder flow with a 5D random viscosity field at mean Re=100 and 500 covered different correlation lengths and in-sample and out-of-sample settings; CDDC-UQ-ROM best reproduced benchmark energy evolution across the cases considered.
watch_item: Reusing the expected-viscosity closure is an approximation, and its reliability beyond the tested 2D cylinder-flow regimes remains unestablished.
paper_title: Data-driven Correction Reduced-Order Stochastic Collocation Method for the Time-Dependent Navier-Stokes Equations
